report.summary: Cause: in public/src/store.js, ship() mutated the existing order object in place and then called set({ orders: state.orders }) with the same array reference. set() skips updates when every changed value is identical by reference, so the view never re-rendered, even though the server update succeeded (hence "Shipped" after a reload). It also held a stale order reference captured before the request. Fix: after the server confirms, ship() builds a new orders list, replacing the matching order (looked up by id in the current state) with a new merged object, so subscribers re-render and the row shows "Shipped" with the button gone. Failure path unchanged: the row keeps its status and "Could not update the order." is shown. Added two store tests (successful ship notifies and updates the row; failed update keeps the row and shows the error). Note: under the Packed filter, a just-shipped row stays visible as "Shipped" until the next load, following ORD-4 literally; ORD-2 could be read as wanting it removed, and the requirements don't say which wins.
report.verification: npm test passes (6/6, including 2 new tests). Also ran the server on spare port 4199 and drove the page with Playwright: clicked "Mark shipped" on ORD-1002 and the row showed "Shipped" with an updated time, no reload. Stopped the server by its process id afterwards.
